analysis.title: Markets Are Puking After Hedges Monetized: Goldman's Derivs Desk Says Buy The Tails Now That Nobody Is Paying For Them
key_insights: Vol was crushed after the midterms. Goldman's Panic Index had its second largest 1-day drop in 20 years (-4.25 on Wednesday, behind -4.68 in 2012-13). VIX closed at 16.61, down 4.22 points (about 20%). VXN fell 18% to 25.08.

The vol crush was universal. NDX Dec fixed strike vol fell more than 3 vol points, RUT Dec almost 2, SPX Dec more than 1. Skew relaxed and vol of vol collapsed. VVIX fell 17 points as investors monetized hedges.
The VIX futures curve, inverted into the vote, reverted to contango (Nov VIX fut 17.74 vs Dec 18).
Vol buyers faded the crush, including a sizable buyer of SPX two-month 30-delta calls (about 1.6 million vega) and four-month 25-delta calls (about 2.5 million vega).

Near-term gamma is cheap. After Wednesday's 113bps straddle realized almost 1.5x to the topside, Thursday's straddle was priced at 59bps and Friday's (payrolls included) at 90bps. The implied move for the rest of the week is 0.80%.

Goldman's CTA model shows about $164bn of SPX selling in a down-tape and about $130bn of buying in an up-tape over the next month, nearly $300bn of potential trend-following flow. Ten days earlier the down-tape figure was $65bn.

The desk sees large distribution tails now that legislative uncertainty has cleared. With net exposures still near lows, it says leveraging options for protection in either direction makes sense and prefers SPX over NDX.

The semis vs hyperscalers rotation was the most prominent theme under the hood. The spread between GSXUHYPR and GSTMTDAT 1-day returns was 9.23%, second largest on record behind DeepSeek Monday (11.02%, January 2025). Apple, Amazon and Microsoft each rose more than 5%.

Goldman prime brokerage data shows Mag7 positioning reset to the 55th percentile vs the past year in late October, opening room to add length. The desk reads lower spending on new capacity as a positive for the free-cash-flow outlook.

Goldman's Delta One desk head Rich Privorotsky wrote that tech flows (at least in Europe) were overwhelmingly bearish and that the market is pricing peak CapEx growth. Goldman's Jeremy Elster said the AI complex is past the peak of good news and in a de-rating cycle.

Thursday morning, S&P e-minis fell about 150 points in roughly 35 minutes from the open on high volume. Bloomberg's Alyce Andres attributed it to programmatic selling, likely CTAs triggered below 7665 per TD Securities. NDX broke back below its 200DMA.

Earnings: about 78% of S&P market cap will have reported by the weekend, with EPS growth on track for 33% y/y. The median beat has outperformed the S&P by 152bps the next day vs a 95bps historical median, but beats among TMT stocks have generally gone unrewarded.

Privorotsky sees vol compression, stable rates and lower oil supporting a constructive grind higher because nets are too low for the market to go down easily. The derivatives desk agrees but does not want to bet on it without a hedge.

Hyperscalers had $31bn of negative free cash flow in Q3. Goldman tallies off-balance-sheet commitments at $1.7tn in leases and $1.9tn in purchase commitments, with $685bn due by end-2027. Goldman thinks moratoria in Texas, Georgia and Michigan could hit 45% of planned data center capacity.
